blocks.summary: What the on-call runbook says now — 3 paragraphs changed

pairs.label: Paging
pairs.before: Every firing of an alert pages the on-call engineer, including a refire of an alert that resolved a moment ago.
pairs.after: Every firing of an alert pages the on-call engineer, except a refire within ten minutes of resolving, which opens its incident without a page.

pairs.label: Paging › Escalation
pairs.after: A refire at a higher severity than the firing it follows always pages, whatever the window says.

pairs.label: Silencing
pairs.before: To stop a flapping alert, silence it by hand for an hour and file a ticket against its rule.
pairs.after: A flapping alert silences itself; silence it by hand only when it flaps for longer than the window.

items.title: The window is per-replica
items.text: Four dispatch replicas each keep their own map, so roughly three quarters of flaps still page and the suppression metric under-reports by the same factor. This is the finding that decides whether the change ships as written.

items.title: Region is not part of the fingerprint
items.text: Same service, two regions, two unrelated failures: the second is suppressed. Adding region is a one-line change and narrows suppression, which is the safe direction.

items.title: The recent map never evicts
items.text: One entry per fingerprint ever seen, held for the life of the process. Bounded in practice by the number of alert rules, which is 3,400 today and not obviously bounded tomorrow.
items.evidence: No eviction path in the file.

items.title: Escalation always pages
items.text: An alert that refires worse than it resolved pages regardless of the window. This is the behaviour the on-call lead asked for and it is implemented correctly.
items.evidence: src/alert/suppress.ts:18, covered by two of the six new tests.

blocks.label: Two regions
blocks.ask: Disk pressure on ledger, instance primary, resolves in eu. A minute later the same rule fires for ledger, instance primary, in us, for an unrelated reason, on the same dispatch replica. With the flag on, does it page?

options.value: No — it is suppressed as a flap
options.because: region is not in IDENTITY, so the us firing shares the eu fingerprint inside the window (W-2)

options.value: Yes — it is a different alert
options.because: they would be, if region were part of the fingerprint; it is not

blocks.label: A worse refire
blocks.ask: An alert resolves as a warning and refires as critical three minutes later. Does it page?

options.because: shouldPage checks escalated before declining as a flap

options.value: No — it is inside the ten-minute window
options.because: the window only suppresses a refire that is not worse than the one before
